```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(sp)
library(geosphere)
```

Import data
```{r}
# import TIRS_SISNAVE data for all possible cases 
suspected_cases <- 
  read.csv("original data/TIRS_SINAVE_combined22_23_blockID.csv")

# import mosquito data
en2 <- read.csv("original data/EN2.csv")

# import enrollment data: initial survey and informed consent
rn1 <- read.csv("original data/RN1.csv")
rn2 <- read.csv("original data/RN2.csv")

# import prospective survey
so1 <- read.csv("original data/SO1.csv")
```

Take relevant data from each file
```{r}
## cases only
case_data <- suspected_cases[suspected_cases$Diagnosis != "Negativo",]

## treatment assignment for each household
trt_assign <- arms_blocks %>% 
  group_by(record_id) %>%
  summarize(arm = mean(a_arm),
            block = mean(a_block))

```



check out data [cases]
  - can we go by lat/lon? seems like yes -- there are households that have both sources so should be fine
```{r}
# households (unique lat/lon) with multiple cases?
case_data %>% 
  group_by(lon, lat) %>%
  summarize(count = n(), .groups = 'keep') %>%
  filter(count != 1)

# does lat/lon work? are there any coordinates that have cases from both sources?
have_both_sources <- case_data %>%
  distinct(lon, lat, Source) %>%
  count(lon, lat) %>%
  filter(n == 2)
## see which households those are -- just to check
case_data %>%
  semi_join(have_both_sources, by = c("lon","lat")) %>%
  arrange(lon, lat) %>%
  select(Source, ID, lat, lon)
## number of cases in those households
case_data %>%
  semi_join(have_both_sources, by = c("lon","lat")) %>%
  group_by(lat, lon) %>%
  summarize(cases_per_household = n(), .groups = 'drop')
```

  - ok wait but what about all the households that just had adult cases?
```{r}
# all SINAVE cases
case_data %>%
  filter(Source == "SINAVE")

# how do these record IDs work???
## find record_id, see how many distinct lat/lon values for each
## these seem to have distinct lon/lat values but the same record_id...should return 0 rows
case_data %>%
  filter(Source == "TIRS") %>%
  mutate(record_id = str_sub(ID, 1,6)) %>% # take the record_id 
  distinct(record_id, lon, lat) %>%
  count(record_id) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

case_data %>%
 # filter(Source == "TIRS") %>%
```

  - more general info
```{r}
# household cases // hh cases, distrib of cases per hh
case_data %>% 
  group_by(lon, lat) %>%
  summarize(cases_per_household = n(), .groups = 'keep') %>%
  group_by(cases_per_household) %>%
  summarize(count = n(), .groups = 'drop')
```
